description: The hand-verified expected outcome for oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/near-sarif-version-only.json. It states a HALT, not rows, despite the .rows.json suffix this folder's naming convention requires -- the suffix names the folder's contract (one expected file per fixture), not the shape of every outcome. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py and harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, never by running the detector and recording what it printed. Where this file and shape.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
null_field_note: tool, scanner_class, adapter and adapter_invoked are null rather than omitted, so a generic loader reads this file with the same keys as the positive expected files in this folder. They are null because the halt precedes tool resolution: a document whose name resolves to no canonical tool has no tool, therefore no scanner_class from the class table and no adapter to route to.

fixture.authored_note: An authored near-SARIF document, not captured tool output: it exists to fail exactly one half of the SARIF conjunction. Its runs object carries an empty results array and an example driver name, so nothing here is a finding, a secret or a Spark path outside the example location its twin uses.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Recorded for parity with the positive expected files in this folder; no row below carries it, because rows is empty by expectation.

shape_detection.conjunction: isinstance(doc, Mapping) and doc.get("version") == "2.1.0" and isinstance(doc.get("runs"), list)
shape_detection.conjunction_authority: AAP 0.5.4: an artifact is SARIF when it carries version "2.1.0" together with a runs array -- those two together are the test.
shape_detection.is_sarif_derivation: The document is a mapping and its version is the exact string "2.1.0", so the first two conditions hold. Its runs value is a JSON object, and isinstance({...}, list) is False, so the third fails and the conjunction is False.
shape_detection.membership_test_note: The runs key is PRESENT and merely of the wrong type. That is deliberate: a detector written as "runs" in doc, or as bool(doc.get("runs")), accepts this document, while the isinstance check shape.is_sarif performs rejects it. This fixture is the one that catches that substitution.
shape_detection.sarif_adapter_invoked_basis: Two independent reasons, either sufficient. First, is_sarif is False, so normalize.shape.route never selects SHARED_SARIF_ADAPTER on the SARIF branch. Second, and decisive for this fixture, route raises before any adapter is selected at all, because the fixture's filename resolves to no canonical tool -- so no adapter module is named and none is imported or called.
shape_detection.counterfactual_note: Recorded so the guarantee is not overclaimed. Routing is keyed by the writing runner's artifact filename, never sniffed from content, and shape.ADAPTER_MODULE_BY_TOOL maps the three SARIF producers to the same shared "sarif" module. So had this document been presented under a recognised producer name it would not halt: it would route with shape "native" -- never "sarif", since is_sarif is False -- and for those three tools the native adapter key happens to be that same shared module. The invariant this fixture pins is therefore the shape decision (never SHAPE_SARIF, RoutingDecision.is_sarif_shape False), and under its own name this fixture reaches no adapter whatsoever.

native_shape_detection.checks_note: The document's four top-level keys are $schema, version, runs and properties. There is no results key at all, so results.failed_checks cannot exist; the top level is an object, so the gitleaks array form and Checkov's multi-framework array form are both excluded.
native_shape_detection.name_resolution_authority: normalize.shape.resolve_tool over the authored tables CANONICAL_TOOLS and ARTIFACT_FILENAME_BY_TOOL in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py. The nine canonical identifiers and nine artifact filenames are not copied here -- shape.py is the single authority, exactly as harness/scope/allowlist.txt is the single authority for the scope globs.
native_shape_detection.name_resolution_note: "near-sarif-version-only.json" is not one of the nine artifact filenames and not one of the nine canonical tool identifiers, so resolve_tool returns None.

halt.reason_note: shape.py names two reasons. This document's top level is a JSON object, which is a supported container, so REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE does not apply; the halt is attributed to the name that resolves to no tool.

observed_attributes.artifact_path_note: Whatever subject the caller passed, echoed unchanged -- route never rewrites it. The value above is the repository-relative fixture path the negative test passes; no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
observed_attributes.stem_note: shape._artifact_name returns PurePath(text).name, so this attribute carries the filename component including its extension rather than a suffix-stripped stem.

halt.sarif_detected_note: False, which is what distinguishes this halt from the other failure UnknownArtifactShape reports: a document that IS valid SARIF appearing under a name harness/artifacts/raw/ must never contain. This one is not valid SARIF, so no such message applies.
halt.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- an artifact matching neither the SARIF shape nor a known native shape is a halt rather than a best-effort parse -- and AAP 0.9.2, which lists it among the conditions that stop the run.

not_a_rejection.reject_classes_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_CLASSES tuple -- a closed set of ten class names, not copied here so the one authority cannot drift into two.
not_a_rejection.statement: The stated outcome is a halt, not a counted rejection: "halt", "UnknownArtifactShape" and "unrecognized-artifact-name" are each provably absent from paths.REJECT_CLASSES, and the test asserts that non-membership programmatically rather than by inspection. A rejection is a per-record outcome inside an adapter that already owns the artifact; this document never reaches an adapter, so there is no record to reject and nothing to count under any class.

parse.note: The fixture is well-formed JSON and json.load succeeds on it. No parser failure is expected here and none is stated: malformed input is a different condition, owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures, and conflating the two would let a JSON syntax error pass as a shape halt.

counts.reconciliation_identity: not applicable -- the halt precedes any record traversal, so no count unit exists to reconcile against

counts_note: raw_finding_records and raw_count_unit are null rather than 0. A count unit is a property of an artifact's known shape -- runs[].results[] for SARIF, Results[].Vulnerabilities[] and its siblings for Trivy -- and this document has no known shape, so there is no unit for normalize.reconcile.count_records to walk. Writing 0 there would assert that a traversal ran and found nothing, which is precisely the empty-result-set reading this fixture exists to prevent. rows and rejections are 0 because nothing was emitted and nothing was rejected.
rows_note: Explicitly empty, and empty for a different reason than a clean scan is empty: the pipeline stopped, it did not look and find nothing.

twin.this_fixture_fails: the runs half -- version is the exact string "2.1.0", but runs is a JSON object rather than an array
twin.twin_fixture_fails: the version half -- runs is a proper array of run objects, but the version string observed in that fixture is "2.1.0-rtm.5", which is not the exact string "2.1.0"
twin.why_the_pair_is_required: Each fixture alone is passed by a defective detector. An implementation testing only version accepts the twin; an implementation testing only runs accepts this one. Only the two together pin the conjunction, so neither expected file is meaningful without the other and each names its twin.
twin.shared_expectation: Both fixtures expect is_sarif False, no adapter invoked, zero rows, zero rejections and a shape.UnknownArtifactShape halt. They differ only in which half of the conjunction fails and in the observed version value the halt report quotes.

guarded_failure: A permissive detector that accepts a non-SARIF document as SARIF does not raise -- it produces an EMPTY RESULT SET, and an empty result set is indistinguishable from a clean scan (AAP 0.5.4). This fixture makes that concrete: a detector that reached the shared SARIF adapter with this document would iterate a runs mapping instead of a runs array, find no run object to read, and report success with zero rows, while its runs.results array is itself empty so even a deeper walk would report nothing. The required outcome is therefore the halt, never a silent zero.
behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture: Row construction of any kind -- no adapter runs, so no field mapping, no severity mapping and no in_scope evaluation is exercised.
Path resolution -- normalize.paths is never called, so no path base, no uriBaseId walk and no non-filesystem coordinate serialisation is exercised.
Per-record rejection -- none of the ten classes in paths.REJECT_CLASSES is reachable from a shape halt.
The other halt reason in shape.py, REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE, which needs a top level that is neither a JSON object nor a JSON array.
The valid-SARIF-under-an-unexpected-name halt, whose sarif_detected attribute is True; this document's is False.
Malformed JSON, owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures.
The reconciliation identity, which has no raw finding record count to assert over here.
prohibitions_observed: No secret value appears in any field of this file (the tree is committed to git). No finding is judged, no finding is deduplicated, and no tool's output is characterised against another's -- this file describes one document's shape detection and nothing else.
